newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Norilsk group loses some state privileges.
newsitem.headline: Russian Norilsk group loses some state privileges.

text.p: A Russian government decree has scrapped some tax privileges for the financially-troubled Norilsk Nickel metals group, Prime-Tass news agency said on Tuesday.

It said Norilsk would no longer have access to a $200 million government credit from foreign sources for equipping certain production facilities. Norilsk would also lose access to state guarantees for commercial bank credits to finance the transport of food to the Arctic, where Norilsk is based.
Prime-Tass gave no reason for the changes.
Norilsk is trying to to win various government privileges and debt relief to ease a financial crisis.

A union leader at Norilsk's flagship plant said earlier on Tuesday that there was still time to avert strikes planned for March 27 and April 2 over wage arrears, but he said formal talks with management had gotten nowhere.
Norilsk owes flagship plant workers around 900 billion roubles in wages unpaid over two months and about 1.2 trillion roubles to various budgets.
Norilsk management has told Moscow that it cannot shoulder the cost of supporting the Arctic towns where its main production facilities are based.
